text_snippet: Exploring the Impact of the Jigsaw Classroom Activity on Student Collaboration, Academic Performance, Attitude, and Anxiety in a Graduate-Level Statistics Course Étude de l'impact de l'activité pédagogique « Jigsaw Classroom » sur la collaboration, les résultats scolaires, l'attitude et l'anxiété des étudiants et des étudiantes dans un cours de statistiques au niveau des cycles supérieurs universitaires Among cooperative learning strategies, the Jigsaw classroom activity is particularly adaptable, working well across diverse age groups and academic disciplines. This strategy is especially relevant in graduate-level statistics courses, which are notoriously difficult and intimidating for non-mathematical students. This qualitative case study explored graduate students’ experiences with the Jigsaw classroom activity in a statistics course within a psychology program. Through semi-structured focus group interviews and reflection papers, participants reflected on the effectiveness of the approach and the challenges encountered. Reflexive thematic analysis identified key themes related to the students’ perceptions and experiences. Pre- and post-survey results indicated a decrease in students’ level of statistical anxiety. title: Evaluation of a Campus-wide Teaching Assistant Training Program Évaluation d’un programme de formation des assistants et des assistantes d’enseignement à l’échelle du campus
text_snippet: Evaluation of a Campus-wide Teaching Assistant Training Program Évaluation d’un programme de formation des assistants et des assistantes d’enseignement à l’échelle du campus Teaching assistants (TAs) play a pivotal role in higher education as they spend a significant amount of time supporting student learning and are often perceived by students as approachable and valuable mentors. In recent years, many large post-secondary institutions have offered centralized teaching assistant training programs, as well as in-depth faculty or department-specific programs. However, despite the acknowledgment of their significance, less is understood regarding the development, delivery, and evaluation of TA training programs, particularly ones that are centralized. This study sought to evaluate a newly developed centralized TA training program to understand the experiences of TAs as well as their perceived needs and recommendations to be able to fulfil their TA duties. This is a mandatory, paid training, and is offered through both in-person and online modules to all first-time teaching assistants across all schools and faculties. A unique component of this program is that the TAs are paid for their training hours. text_snippet: Self-Regulated Learning Skills Contribute to Academic Success and Academic Resilience in First-Year Students Enrolled in an Online Physiology Course Les compétences en matière d'apprentissage autonome contribuent à la réussite scolaire et à la résilience académique des étudiants et des étudiantes de première année inscrits à un cours de physiologie en ligne Self-regulated learners can independently plan, carry out, and evaluate their own learning process, and self-regulated learning (SRL) is positively associated with academic success. However, youth, limited post-secondary experience, and online delivery are all factors independently associated with poorer SRL skills. Since the COVID-19 pandemic, online course offerings have flourished, creating unprecedented challenges for first-year undergraduate students. Using a mixed-method approach, this study examined how SRL attitudes and behaviours contributed to the success and/or resilience of students enrolled in an online introductory physiology course. SRL skills were significantly associated with students’ final grades. High-achieving students also planned to use more learning strategies that are supported by evidence compared to their lower-achieving peers. title: Do Nursing Students Who Practice Self-care Activities Experience Fewer Feelings of Anxiety and Stress? Les étudiants et les étudiantes en soins infirmiers qui pratiquent des activités d'autogestion de la santé ressentent-ils moins d'anxiété et de stress ?
text_snippet: Do Nursing Students Who Practice Self-care Activities Experience Fewer Feelings of Anxiety and Stress? Les étudiants et les étudiantes en soins infirmiers qui pratiquent des activités d'autogestion de la santé ressentent-ils moins d'anxiété et de stress ? Nursing schools are known for their combination of demanding academic requirements and often stressful clinical experiences. Nursing instructors at a polytechnic in western Canada noted ongoing concerns with nursing students struggling to manage their anxiety. The goal of this study was to understand if self-care activities introduced during each clinical rotation day would help to reduce feelings of anxiety and stress in second- and third-year nursing students. Nursing instructor participants were given a list of the four self-care activities (gratitude list, deep breathing, journalling, and colouring) to be explained and practiced at the end of each clinical day. At the end of the completed clinical session, the participating nursing students and nursing instructors were given a questionnaire to complete during their final post-conference regarding the effectiveness of the self-care activities. Braun and Clark’s framework for thematic analysis was employed to answer the research objective. title: The Attitudes of First Year Health Students towards Indigenous People and Engaging in Mandatory Indigenous Courses Attitudes des étudiants et des étudiantes de première année en sciences de la santé envers les peuples autochtones et leur participation aux cours obligatoires sur les peuples autochtones
text_snippet: The Attitudes of First Year Health Students towards Indigenous People and Engaging in Mandatory Indigenous Courses Attitudes des étudiants et des étudiantes de première année en sciences de la santé envers les peuples autochtones et leur participation aux cours obligatoires sur les peuples autochtones The purpose of this research was to explore undergraduate students’ attitudes towards Indigenous People, Indigenous health care, and how students feel about having to engage in mandatory Indigenous course content. Studies have demonstrated that taking courses with Indigenous content improves cultural competency, thereby improving the overall health outcomes of Indigenous people (Stansfield & Browne, 2012). The exploration of student attitudes toward mandatory Indigenous content is a novel area of study. Health students were interviewed using a semi-structured interview guide. Data was processed using thematic analysis. Student attitudes towards Indigenous people could inform how students feel about engaging in mandatory Indigenous courses. text_snippet: Transdisciplinary Pedagogical Strategies for Complex Problems: A Scoping Review Stratégies pédagogiques transdisciplinaires pour les problèmes complexes : une étude exploratoire Wicked or complex problems pose significant negative consequences on human, animal, and environmental health. Some wicked problems such as climate change are considered “super wicked” as their impacts worsen over time, making them even more challenging and urgent to address. The One Health approach has been widely recognized as a promising method for addressing complex problems by promoting the collaboration between different disciplines and stakeholders. There is a need to train health professionals to appropriately apply the One Health approach to better address and help mitigate the effects of complex problems. The aim of this scoping review was to identify pedagogical strategies that promote integration of multiple disciplines and perspectives to address complex problems in classrooms across Canada and the United States of America. Five databases were searched for relevant literature, with primary research articles published in 2016 or later being eligible for review. The search yielded 6,552 articles, with 22 articles ultimately being eligible for inclusion. text_snippet: Critical Reflection on Educator Experiences of Negotiated Grading Réflexion critique sur les expériences des enseignants et des enseignantes en matière de notation négociée The paper “Critical Reflection on Educator Experiences of Negotiated Grading” reports on an alternative grading system in higher education. Instead of the traditional method where the teacher solely decides grades, this “negotiated grading” system involves students in the grading process. Educators from nursing and business disciplines shared their experiences with this approach.

text_snippet: From Anxiety to Engagement: Transforming Social Work Research Education De l'anxiété à l'engagement : transformer l'enseignement de la recherche en travail social In this study, we explore the transformation of social work students from experiencing research anxiety to active engagement in research conducted within a mandatory course at a leading Canadian university. Traditionally, many social workers have perceived a distinct divide between practical social work and academic research, often viewing research methodologies as intimidating and unrelated to their professional responsibilities. The course was reformatted to help students view research as integral to effective social work and consider themselves as potential researchers. text_snippet: A Study on Faculty Beliefs and Teaching Practices for Student Wellbeing Étude sur les convictions et les pratiques pédagogiques des enseignants et des enseignantes en matière de bien-être des étudiants et des étudiantes This study, conducted at a North American research-intensive university with two campuses, examined the relationship between faculty beliefs and teaching practices concerning student wellbeing. Drawing on results from a 2023 institutional survey (17.9% response rate), the research questions explored whether faculty believe their teaching practices influence student wellbeing, whether they employ wellbeing-focused practices, and if their beliefs align with their actions. Findings revealed that respondents overwhelmingly believed (92%) that their teaching practices impact student wellbeing. In terms of practices, a majority of faculty reported discussing wellbeing topics (55%) and sharing wellbeing resources (52%) within their class. At the same time, some differences were found in the adoption of wellbeing strategies based on years of teaching experience and course level. In terms of alignment, a statistically significant association was found between faculty beliefs about their impact on student wellbeing and whether they employ wellbeing practices in class. title: Using Formative Feedback to Teach Pharmacy Students to Write Critical Self-reflections Utilisation du retour d'information formatif pour apprendre aux étudiants et aux étudiantes en pharmacie à rédiger des réflexions critiques sur leur propre pratique
text_snippet: Using Formative Feedback to Teach Pharmacy Students to Write Critical Self-reflections Utilisation du retour d'information formatif pour apprendre aux étudiants et aux étudiantes en pharmacie à rédiger des réflexions critiques sur leur propre pratique Critical thinking is an essential skill for practising pharmacists. Critical self-reflections have been said to contribute to critical thinking, and formative feedback has been cited as improving student learning. We conducted a two-year study, using mixed methods research, with two cohorts of 1st to 4th year pharmacy students, 76 students in total, to improve their critical self-reflective skills as part of critical thinking. Our pedagogical approaches, unlike the pedagogy of didactic teaching that is historically associated with health professional education, included the writing of critical self-reflections and the use of formative assessment. Students wrote eight self-reflections over four semesters. We provided formative feedback after each self-reflection, which included individual written comments and whole class formative feedback during an explicit instruction class. However, to strengthen the study design we did not provide any feedback between the first and second reflections. title: Fostering Student Collaboration in an Online Asynchronous Problem-based Learning Webtool Favoriser la collaboration entre étudiants et étudiantes grâce à un outil web d'apprentissage par problèmes asynchrone en ligne
text_snippet: Fostering Student Collaboration in an Online Asynchronous Problem-based Learning Webtool Favoriser la collaboration entre étudiants et étudiantes grâce à un outil web d'apprentissage par problèmes asynchrone en ligne The scholarly landscape is shifting towards online knowledge production and consumption. Understanding the effect this digital shift has on teaching in practical and collaboration-based contexts is timely since many online applications and webtools are being developed to promote student engagement in asynchronous online courses across a variety of disciplines. The Virtual Mystery (VM) webtool was created for large in-person courses to provide online asynchronous student collaboration in the form of hybridized problem-based learning case studies to small groups of students. This study examines the impact of course delivery (online vs blended) on these group collaborations and quality of work for the VM webtool. This paper analyzes anonymous student survey data from six iterations of a large first-year archaeology and biological anthropology course with two different modalities (online vs blended). title: Exploring Student Motivation for Incorporating APA Citation Guidelines Étude de la motivation des étudiants et des étudiantes à appliquer les directives de citation de l'APA
text_snippet: Exploring Student Motivation for Incorporating APA Citation Guidelines Étude de la motivation des étudiants et des étudiantes à appliquer les directives de citation de l'APA Despite the widespread use of the American Psychological Association (APA) citations and referencing guidelines in undergraduate courses, students continue to make errors, perceiving the task of incorporating these guidelines as burdensome and tedious. To support students’ use of the guidelines, various aids have been developed, such as online citation generators, workshops, and handouts, with mixed results. One avenue to examine the errors students are making with the APA guidelines is to explore their motivation. Utilizing Situated Expectancy-Value Theory as our theoretical framework, we explored student motivation for incorporating the APA guidelines into their work, focusing on the components of expectancy, value, and cost. One hundred and fifty-five undergraduate students completed our online survey and indicated high expectancy and value and midline cost when considering implementing the APA guidelines into their assignments. Yet, when provided with an APA referencing task to complete, perceptions of expectancy and value dropped significantly. title: Decolonization of Academic Practices in Canadian Universities: Non-Indigenous Students as Allies Décolonisation des pratiques académiques dans les universités canadiennes : les étudiants et les étudiantes non autochtones comme alliés
text_snippet: Decolonization of Academic Practices in Canadian Universities: Non-Indigenous Students as Allies Décolonisation des pratiques académiques dans les universités canadiennes : les étudiants et les étudiantes non autochtones comme alliés Non-Indigenous graduate students can play an important role in decolonizing academic practices, thereby supporting post-secondary institutions’ efforts to Indigenize learning in Canada. Preparing non-Indigenous students to unlearn colonizing practices and obtaining their proactive contribution, therefore, remains an urgent task. Against this background, the following interrelated questions have been examined: how do non-Indigenous graduate students understand the meaning and purpose of Indigenization of learning? How do current academic strategies prepare non-Indigenous students to participate in decolonizing practices? An online survey with 10 questions was administered among non-Indigenous graduate students at a research-intensive university in Southwestern Ontario. A total of 42 students participated in the survey. The data were thematically analyzed in three major areas, including a) content, b) teaching method, and c) participation in community-based practices. title: Horses as the Classroom: Empathetic Leadership Development via a Pedagogical Experiment and Social Enterprise Partnership Les chevaux comme salle de classe : le développement du leadership empathique à travers une expérience pédagogique et un partenariat avec une entreprise sociale
text_snippet: Horses as the Classroom: Empathetic Leadership Development via a Pedagogical Experiment and Social Enterprise Partnership Les chevaux comme salle de classe : le développement du leadership empathique à travers une expérience pédagogique et un partenariat avec une entreprise sociale Can we be changemakers without empathy? If we seek to build tomorrow’s leaders, do we need to rethink leadership education to support the growth of the next generations’ changemakers? This exploratory research partnership explored students’ empathetic leadership capabilities through an out-of-classroom learning experience with a social enterprise providing equine-assisted coaching (n=17). Students subsequently participated in a post-event survey to assess their capabilities and their interpretation of the experience’s impact (n=8). Results, while preliminary, suggest that students gained awareness of their capabilities through self-reflection and saw the need for strengthening, even if they did not report uniform growth in those capabilities. This strongly suggests current approaches to building empathetic leadership skills in post-secondary education require reconsideration. Additionally, this research partnership highlights significant ongoing barriers to meaningful community engagement, including academic culture, timelines, and success metrics.

Points de vue des enseignants, des enseignantes, des étudiants et des étudiantes We investigated perceptions of a longstanding undergraduate course grade alignment policy in a large psychology department at a large research-oriented university. Reflexive Thematic Analysis of instructor interviews and student focus groups led to developing six themes revealing the policy’s perceived impact on teaching and learning practices. Discussion emphasizes three major findings. First, this policy influences how instructors design and deliver courses; implementation differences have consequences for students. Second, instructors and students alike worry about this policy’s impact on grades perceived beyond the institution. Third, participants situate this policy in a dynamic and relational ethical landscape, connecting it to systemic barriers to inclusion, fairness, trust, and authenticity. title: Revisiting the 4M Framework: Canadian SoTL in a Post-Pandemic World Réexamen du cadre 4M : l’avancement des connaissances en enseignement et en apprentissage (ACEA) au Canada dans un monde post-pandémique
text_snippet: Revisiting the 4M Framework: Canadian SoTL in a Post-Pandemic World Réexamen du cadre 4M : l’avancement des connaissances en enseignement et en apprentissage (ACEA) au Canada dans un monde post-pandémique The Scholarship of Teaching and Learning (SoTL) in Canada has significantly transformed since the COVID-19 pandemic. Through the lens of the 4M (micro-meso-macro-mega) Framework, this scholarly personal narrative discusses the factors that impact the advancement of Canadian SoTL post-pandemic from the perspectives of seven scholars of varying rank and position from seven universities across Canada. Our collective insights highlight the unique opportunities and challenges for SoTL work at the individual, departmental/program, institutional, and beyond-institutional levels, that both emerged and persisted following the COVID-19 pandemic. We discuss practical suggestions, such as leveraging technology including generative AI and working collaboratively, for the continued advancement of Canadian SoTL in the post-pandemic higher education landscape.

title: Apprentissage hybride de la psychologie en contexte universitaire : Efficacité et perspectives étudiantes Blended Learning of Psychology in University Classes: Efficacy and Student Perspectives
text_snippet: Apprentissage hybride de la psychologie en contexte universitaire : Efficacité et perspectives étudiantes Blended Learning of Psychology in University Classes: Efficacy and Student Perspectives L’utilisation du format hybride pour l’enseignement en contexte universitaire est à la hausse, cependant, peu d’études ont observé son efficacité auprès des étudiants et recueilli leurs points de vue à cet égard, spécifiquement dans le domaine de la psychologie. Le but de cet article est donc de documenter des études dont l’objet porte sur l’utilisation des cours hybrides en psychologie de premier cycle à l’université. Les objectifs sont de recenser les études qui ont porté sur 1) la relation entre les cours hybrides de premier cycle en psychologie et la performance universitaire des étudiants ainsi que 2) sur leurs perceptions et leur niveau de satisfaction vis-à-vis les cours hybrides et 3) sur les facteurs pouvant contribuer à la réussite et à une expérience positive en contexte de cours hybride. Malgré le nombre limité d’études recensées, les résultats sont prometteurs pour l’enseignement hybride de la psychologie au niveau universitaire.

title: Accessibility of University Campuses: Helping Undergraduates Better Understand, and Advocate for, Accessibility Accessibilité des campus universitaires : aider les étudiants et les étudiantes de premier cycle à mieux comprendre les questions d’accessibilité et à plaider pour l’accessibilité
text_snippet: Accessibility of University Campuses: Helping Undergraduates Better Understand, and Advocate for, Accessibility Accessibilité des campus universitaires : aider les étudiants et les étudiantes de premier cycle à mieux comprendre les questions d’accessibilité et à plaider pour l’accessibilité In this paper, a research project within a newly developed upper-level Applied Psychology course is described. The intent of the course project was to improve undergraduate students’ understanding of disability and accessibility. An authentic learning approach was used to engage students in two key activities: a) conducting a physical accessibility audit of the entrances to high-traffic buildings on campus and the pathways leading to them; and b) surveying the campus to better understand perceptions of campus accessibility and priorities for change. Student researchers used the audit and survey data to identify changes that could improve campus accessibility. The aims of this paper are twofold. One, to describe a course research project on accessibility, and reflect on the project’s successes and limitations, so it could be adapted for use by other instructors. Two, to evaluate how the course research project impacted student learning.

title: Sharing Indigenous Knowledges in University Teaching: The Need for Conciliable Spaces Partager les savoirs autochtones dans l'enseignement universitaire : la nécessité d'espaces conciliables
text_snippet: Sharing Indigenous Knowledges in University Teaching: The Need for Conciliable Spaces Partager les savoirs autochtones dans l'enseignement universitaire : la nécessité d'espaces conciliables Calls to Indigenize the curriculum have been occurring and, indeed, increasing across Canadian universities since the release in 2015 of the calls to action of the Truth and Reconciliation Commission (TRC, 2015). The present article documents the emergence at two universities of a support program for Indigenous curriculum, in the form of digital Indigenous Learning Bundles. The Indigenous Learning Bundles model was first conceptualized in 2018 by Kanien’kehá:ka (Mohawk) scholar Kahente Horn-Miller of Carleton University, in Ottawa, Canada, and was later adopted in 2021 by an Indigenous-led curriculum development team at Western University. Both projects involve deep collaborations between Indigenous and non-Indigenous people and strive to unite people around the ethical inclusion of Indigenous knowledge in a post-secondary setting. The bundles involve the co-creation of a collection of Indigenous-led digital teaching resources that prioritize local Indigenous knowledges and ethics in the making and delivering of learning opportunities in classrooms. title: Instructors’ Consideration of Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion in the Urgent Transition to Online Teaching Considérations des enseignants et des enseignantes sur l'équité, la diversité et l'inclusion dans le cadre de la transition urgente vers l'enseignement en ligne
text_snippet: Instructors’ Consideration of Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion in the Urgent Transition to Online Teaching Considérations des enseignants et des enseignantes sur l'équité, la diversité et l'inclusion dans le cadre de la transition urgente vers l'enseignement en ligne In the urgent move from conventional classrooms to online learning made necessary by the COVID-19 pandemic, teachers in higher education made hard choices about pedagogy, student support, ethical responsibilities to professions and disciplines, and a host of other considerations. Equity, diversity, and inclusion (EDI) are fundamental and explicit values expressed by institutions of higher education, despite recent controversy and backlash surrounding the complex construct (Walk-Morris, 2024; Yang, 2024). This study asked whether EDI came into conscious play for higher education teachers when they moved their classes online, and if so, how EDI was expressed in course re-designs, delivery, and assessment. Findings revealed explicit tensions around EDI issues, and instructors expressed EDI values in their courses, but they identified fewer specific course design and delivery choices made to promote EDI.

text_snippet: Bringing Teamwork and Experiential Learning to Large First Year Classes: The UTSC Approach and the Student Perspective Introduire le travail d'équipe et l'apprentissage par l'expérience dans les grandes classes de première année : l'approche de l'UTSC et le point de vue des étudiants et des étudiantes Experiential learning and having students work in teams are two educational contexts that allow students to exercise the sorts of skills that bring success in post-graduation life: skills like critical and creative thought, effective communication and collaboration, and the ability to not only see one’s strengths and weakness, but also the skills needed to grow personally. Typically, these sorts of experiences are only offered in smaller upper-year courses simply because of the logistics involved in managing such work. This paper argues that the development of such skills is too important to wait until third or fourth year, especially given the accelerated advance in AI technologies which make these human skills more important than ever to student success. In this report, the University of Toronto Scarborough Approach to Teamwork and Experiential Learning is described, which works even with extremely large first-year courses. title: A Redesign of a Clinical Evaluation Tool to Promote Clear Expectations and Reflective Practice Une refonte d'un outil d'évaluation clinique pour promouvoir des attentes claires et une pratique réflexive
text_snippet: A Redesign of a Clinical Evaluation Tool to Promote Clear Expectations and Reflective Practice Une refonte d'un outil d'évaluation clinique pour promouvoir des attentes claires et une pratique réflexive Clinical practice is complex and requires a consistent assessment process to effectively navigate student evaluation. Nursing programs must ensure that assessment methods measure entry-to-practice competencies. A clear description of expectations and a consistent approach to the evaluation of student performance is required. A quality improvement project was conducted to modify existing practices for evaluating student clinical performance. The Quality and Safety Education for Nurses competencies were used as a foundation for a redesigned clinical evaluation tool using standardized behavioural indicators and a complementary weekly reflection and anecdotal notes document (RAND). Two priorities guided the redesign: clear expectations and building capacity for reflection. The redesigned evaluation tool and associated RAND provide clear expectations for student behaviour in practice, a foundation for comprehensive feedback, and a means to build capacity for student reflection.

title: Lessons Learned from Faculty and Students' Perceptions of Remote Learning Leçons tirées des perceptions des enseignants, des enseignantes, des étudiants et des étudiantes sur l'apprentissage à distance
text_snippet: Lessons Learned from Faculty and Students' Perceptions of Remote Learning Leçons tirées des perceptions des enseignants, des enseignantes, des étudiants et des étudiantes sur l'apprentissage à distance Remote learning brought with it challenges for both learners and educators alike. While some in higher education are keen to return to “how things were,” we believe that remote learning brought with it lessons that should be implemented into post-pandemic teaching. We sought to investigate what components of online/blended learning approaches both learners and educators would like to see continue in a post-pandemic era, as well as identify supports needed for faculty to successfully implement online/blended learning. Using a sequential explanatory mixed-methods approach, we collected data from students and faculty across one School in a variety of programs (undergraduate, graduate, professional). Using thematic analysis and descriptive statistics, we found that while remote learning was challenging in terms of educator/learner engagement and social isolation, both educators and learners identified that remote learning helped with the development of time management skills, and flexibility in schedule planning. title: Trauma-informed Pedagogical Practices in Post-Secondary Education: An Integrative Review of the Literature Pratiques pédagogiques tenant compte des traumatismes dans l'enseignement postsecondaire : revue intégrative des publications de recherche
text_snippet: Trauma-informed Pedagogical Practices in Post-Secondary Education: An Integrative Review of the Literature Pratiques pédagogiques tenant compte des traumatismes dans l'enseignement postsecondaire : revue intégrative des publications de recherche The experience of past or current trauma can interfere with learning in post-secondary education and can be particularly problematic for people from equity-deserving groups. Implementing trauma-informed pedagogical practices could contribute significantly to post-secondary education by cultivating safe and equitable learning spaces that support a range of needs and potentially lead to better academic outcomes. However, the uptake of trauma-informed pedagogy in post-secondary institutions has lagged despite increased attention to students’ experience of trauma. Post-secondary educators may not be aware of trauma-informed pedagogical practices or know how to implement them. Currently there are few comprehensive resources for about trauma-informed pedagogy. The purpose of this paper is to report on the findings of an integrative review of the literature conducted to gather and categorize information regarding trauma-informed pedagogical practices in post-secondary education. text_snippet: Enhanced Conceptual Learning with Real Time Student-Generated Data and Visualization Apprentissage conceptuel amélioré grâce à des données générées en temps réel par les élèves et à leur visualisation Interactive student response systems (SRS, clickers) are used in post-secondary classrooms to enhance student engagement and learning. Their use, however, is most often limited to reviewing material with multiple choice questions. The present study examined student responses to a strategy for technology-enhanced learning within an introductory understanding research course to improve student experiences. SMART Technologies Interactive Response System™ was used to collect anonymous student data during classes, with raw data exportation into a Microsoft Excel™ spreadsheet coupled with Tableau Data Visualization software. Students engaged with statistical concepts through their own real-time data generation and immediate visualization, as well as participated in discussions of concepts with their peers and instructor. Students gave positive feedback on the use of clickers in this novel application. The unique combination of technologies provided a fast and powerful means of illustrating student-generated data and encouraged critical thinking and student engagement and enjoyment. title: Reflective Learning in Education Courses: Conceptualizations and Instructional Strategies L'apprentissage réflexif dans les cours d'éducation : conceptualisations et stratégies pédagogiques
text_snippet: Reflective Learning in Education Courses: Conceptualizations and Instructional Strategies L'apprentissage réflexif dans les cours d'éducation : conceptualisations et stratégies pédagogiques Reflective learning is considered crucial for advancing learning strategies, improving professional practice, and engaging in lifelong learning. For this reason, developing reflective learning has been imperative for the education of professionals across disciplines. Despite its potential, however, there is a lack of conceptual clarity and models of good practice for developing students’ reflective skills. The purpose of this study is to review conceptualizations of reflective learning and related instructional strategies. We conducted a scoping review of 53 empirical studies obtained through a search of Education Source, ERIC, and PsycInfo databases. The results indicate a range of conceptualizations of reflective learning including content understanding, evaluation of perspectives, review of practice, metacognition, and examination of sociocultural contexts of education. Instructional strategies are discussed in terms of objects and process of reflection. We propose a conceptualization of reflective learning that goes beyond developing professional competencies to addressing broader issues relevant to everyday life.

title: An Examination of Canadian Post-Secondary Faculty Beliefs Concerning Learning Strategies Examen des croyances des professeurs et des professeures de niveau postsecondaire au Canada concernant les stratégies d'apprentissage
text_snippet: An Examination of Canadian Post-Secondary Faculty Beliefs Concerning Learning Strategies Examen des croyances des professeurs et des professeures de niveau postsecondaire au Canada concernant les stratégies d'apprentissage Students make many decisions in academia concerning learning. One of the most critical among them is what learning strategy to use. This research surveyed faculty members from various Canadian colleges and universities to examine their opinions on the effectiveness of different learning strategies. Although the results were mixed, the overall finding showed a discrepancy between faculty opinions and best evidence. Several demographic factors were examined (for example, the faculty’s highest degree, employment status, number of years teaching, subject taught, and institution type), but none was a meaningful predictor of faculty opinions regarding learning strategy effectiveness. Even though faculty opinions were not in line with recognized evidence, their views provide insight into the learning strategies perceived as beneficial and those that students may be using. Learning is a complicated process that can be affected by numerous factors. Hence, this paper reports on the opinions of Canadian faculty concerning learning strategies that facilitate this process and presents plausible theories to explain the disconnect between their views and the best evidence.

Consequently, writers’ identities can be inferred by their readers as similar to the writers’ intended identities or distinctively. Such identity inferences of the author can play a vital role in readers’ perception and evaluation of a written work. Nonetheless, the instructors’ perceptions of multilingual student writers’ (MSWs) identities who write in English as their additional language have received little attention in the literature. Therefore, this study initially examined the academic writer identity constructions of five undergraduate MSWs in the Canadian context. Second, the extent to which instructor-readers construct these MSWs’ academic writer identities was explored. Finally, I examined whether there are discrepancies or similarities between the academic writer identities that student-participants intended to project in their text and the identity that instructor-participants constructed. title: Rethinking Classroom Management from a Student-Centered Perspective: An Online Module Approach Repenser la gestion de classe dans une perspective centrée sur l'élève : une approche par module en ligne
text_snippet: Rethinking Classroom Management from a Student-Centered Perspective: An Online Module Approach Repenser la gestion de classe dans une perspective centrée sur l'élève : une approche par module en ligne In our qualitative research study, we sought to determine whether completing a set of online modules called Classroom Flow could shift pre-service teachers’ (PSTs’) perceptions, language, and practice towards developing classroom cultures that are more student-centered. The online modules encouraged PSTs to familiarize themselves with the various classroom management theories and practices throughout history. Embedded case study scenarios within the modules enabled PSTs to encounter, redirect, and/or mitigate off-task student behaviours in a safe environment outside of the classroom. Throughout the modules, we opted to use the language of flow to represent the idea of classroom management from a more student-centered perspective. Our findings revealed that the use of online modules not only enabled PSTs to reflect on their choices for establishing student-centered classroom cultures and mitigating classroom disruptions but also helped to fill a gap in their teacher education programs.

title: Community Engaged Learning in Challenging Contexts: Introducing and Assessing a Flexible Model for CEL in a First-Year Cohort Program L'apprentissage communautaire dans des contextes difficiles : introduction et évaluation d'un modèle flexible de l’apprentissage communautaire dans un programme de cohorte de première année
text_snippet: Community Engaged Learning in Challenging Contexts: Introducing and Assessing a Flexible Model for CEL in a First-Year Cohort Program L'apprentissage communautaire dans des contextes difficiles : introduction et évaluation d'un modèle flexible de l’apprentissage communautaire dans un programme de cohorte de première année Community Engaged Learning (CEL) is an increasingly popular and celebrated pedagogy in post-secondary education. Research indicates that CEL supports students’ academic engagement, strengthens their professional skills, and provides them with an enhanced sense of civic responsibility. CEL is labour-intensive, though, and many instructors seek light-touch options as a way of integrating CEL in particularly challenging environments—for example in first-year, multidisciplinary, or large-class settings. This article presents a flexible model of CEL developed in such a challenging setting: we share results from our effort to bring CEL to a multi-course, multi-disciplinary program for first-year students. Our experience shows an adaptable way forward for CEL that could be applied in varied educational settings; we share insights into what we learned, including where we can improve, in our efforts to develop large-scale CEL.

title: Exploring the Theoretical Foundations, Claims, and Caveats of the Design Principles for Multimedia Learning in Higher Education Exploration des fondements théoriques, des affirmations et des mises en garde concernant les principes de conception de l'apprentissage multimédia dans l'enseignement supérieur
text_snippet: Exploring the Theoretical Foundations, Claims, and Caveats of the Design Principles for Multimedia Learning in Higher Education Exploration des fondements théoriques, des affirmations et des mises en garde concernant les principes de conception de l'apprentissage multimédia dans l'enseignement supérieur Multimedia learning takes place when people learn from images and words together. Research and theory from cognitive psychology, social psychology, and instructional design have all been used to propose and investigate specific design principles for effective multimedia learning. Research has demonstrated that applying even one of these principles can have an enormous impact on participants’ learning outcomes, producing large effect sizes on tests of memory and transfer or application of knowledge. The literature suggests that applying multiple principles at once will produce tremendous benefits for student learning and motivation. But while courses are messy and complicated, most of the research on multimedia design principles has been conducted in highly controlled, one-session experiments testing one principle at a time. Curriculum and instructional design both involve a multitude of variables. What impact do these principles have in the context of all of the other decisions that instructors make? text_snippet: Student Achievement of Institutional Learning Outcomes: Case Study of a Regional University in Western Canada Réalisation des résultats d'apprentissage institutionnels par les étudiants et les étudiantes : étude de cas d'une université régionale de l'Ouest canadien Considerable attention has been paid to postsecondary students’ higher-order skill development, which has students, parents, employers, and politicians questioning the value of a university degree. Agreement over an essential common core of knowledge or skill sets cuts across the liberal education and employment education divide. Both sides agree that for life fulfillment and career success, students require literacy, numeracy, problem solving, critical thinking, and (intercultural) communication skills. Yet, assessing these types of complex qualitative skills has persistently presented as a significant challenge, with no clear guidance for postsecondary institutions. This paper presents a case study of a mid-sized regional university in Western Canada that has undertaken a multi-phased action research project to evaluate institutional learning outcomes using course-embedded capstone research papers in science and professional baccalaureate degree programs. text_snippet: What WIL We Do? The result of all this activity has been a rise in the need to discuss WIL curriculum design, particularly as it pertains to student preparation before a WIL experience (Cooper et al., 2010). title: Implementing Diverse Continuous Reflective Strategies in a Multi-Section General Chemistry II Lab Mise en œuvre de diverses stratégies de réflexion continue dans un laboratoire de chimie générale II à sections multiples
text_snippet: Implementing Diverse Continuous Reflective Strategies in a Multi-Section General Chemistry II Lab Mise en œuvre de diverses stratégies de réflexion continue dans un laboratoire de chimie générale II à sections multiples Chemistry labs are often taught using a rote mechanical approach without much explicit scaffolding for academic reflection by the students. Reflection, however, can play an essential role in learning because it is an evidence-based learning process that generates, deepens, critiques, and documents learning. By moving away from traditional teaching approaches and emphasizing reflection, the first-year chemistry lab could support students in developing more diverse skills, a growth mindset, and greater engagement. The current study, which represents phase four of a multi-year project, explores first-year students’ attitudes toward reflective learning in a chemistry laboratory setting that focuses explicitly on supporting reflection. Two creative student-directed inquiry-based experiments were redesigned and implemented with diverse reflective strategies in order to support students’ sense-making skills and stimulate their understanding of scientific concepts. Data were collected using surveys and students’ reflective artifacts. text_snippet: Supporting Self-regulated Learning across Disciplines in International Post-secondary Education Soutenir l'apprentissage auto-dirigé dans toutes les disciplines de l'enseignement supérieur international This paper reports on the results of a project involving the incorporation of Self-Regulated Learning Supportive Practices (SRL-SPs) in required first-year courses for new international students at Vantage College, a specialized pathway program at The University of British Columbia.
